title: Planner: private tasks stored in your private plan instead of Microsoft To Do
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, automatic enablement, storage change and Teams controls are supported. Two minor licensing clarifications remain: qualify Microsoft 365 entitlement and distinguish the notice's task-history statement from the service description's licensed availability.

claims.where: front matter: title, products; What's changing
claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns Microsoft Planner private tasks.
claims.quote: "title": "Planner: Private tasks now stored in your private plan", "products": ["Planner"]

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk, impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to store new private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences in the user's private Planner plan instead of the Microsoft To Do task store.
claims.quote: Beginning in December 2026, private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences will be stored in a user's own private Planner plan instead of the Microsoft To Do task store.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the private plan as a single place for the user's private tasks.
claims.quote: Private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences are stored in the user’s private plan, providing a single place for tasks visible only to that user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure, Security & identity
claims.claim: Private tasks remain visible only to the task owner.
claims.quote: Private tasks remain visible only to the task owner and cannot be shared or assigned to others.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Private tasks cannot be shared with others.
claims.quote: Private tasks cannot be shared or assigned to others, and existing tasks continue to work and appear alongside them.

claims.quote: existing tasks continue to work and appear alongside them.

claims.quote: This enables richer Planner capabilities, such as labels and task history, while maintaining the same private experience.
claims.fix: Keep the notice attribution and add: 'The Planner service description separately lists task history as included with Planner and Project Plan 3 and Microsoft 365 Copilot, but not with Microsoft 365 alone or Planner Plan 1.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-planner-service-description, whose Task history row is No / No / Yes / Yes. Do not imply every user receives task history.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Which Power Automate connector applies to the new private tasks is not explicitly documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "private plan" "Power Automate" "Graph". Read manage-planner-app and connectors/planner; the latter supports basic plans only and does not identify the new private plan as basic or name a connector for this change.

claims.claim: Which Microsoft Graph APIs reach tasks in the new private plan remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "private plan" "Power Automate" "Graph". Read graph/planner-concept-overview and search excerpts for graph/api/resources/planner. These give general plan/task operations, not explicit support for this new private-plan experience.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The storage change is an included option within the existing licensed Planner product, with no separate entitlement published for the change.
claims.quote: Users with a qualifying Microsoft 365 license have access to a rich set of capabilities for individual and team work management. These capabilities include basic plan creation and editing capabilities, task creation and editing capabilities

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Teams Planner page says users with a Microsoft 365 licence are entitled to the Planner app.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft 365 license are entitled to the Planner app.
claims.fix: Replace the broad entitlement sentence in licensing.notes and Cost and licensing with: 'Users with a qualifying Microsoft 365 licence have access to Planner task creation and editing and My Tasks; the Planner for admins page lists the eligible subscriptions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/planner/planner-for-admins, which explicitly qualifies entitlement as 'qualifying' and 'eligible'; the cited Teams page gives the broader wording.

claims.where: controls[0].ui, controls[0].api; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No administrator UI or API switch is documented to retain new Planner private tasks in To Do instead of the private Planner plan.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "private tasks" "private plan" disable opt out Microsoft To Do storage. Read manage-planner-app, disable-planner, planner-for-admins and FAQ. General app restrictions and Project task sync are not a switch retaining these new private tasks in To Do.

claims.claim: Tenant-wide Planner app availability in Teams is controlled at Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block.
claims.quote:
In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps.

To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> in the MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module changes the Teams app's tenant state.
claims.quote:
Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module
Update-M365TeamsApp
    -Id <String>
    [-IsBlocked <Boolean>]
-Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app.
-IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference examples describe -IsBlocked $true as unblocking.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: The Teams app blocking control governs app availability in Teams, not the choice of private-task storage or a way to keep tasks in To Do.
claims.quote: Planner is enabled by default for all Teams users in your organization. You can turn off or turn on the app at the org level on the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.
